newsitem.title: UK: Russia's SBS-AGRO ups Eurobond amid strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Russia's SBS-AGRO ups Eurobond amid strong demand.

text.p: SBS-AGRO, one of Russia's largest private banks, increased its debut Eurobond for the second time on Thursday amid strong demand, lead manager JP Morgan said.
"We have been seeing excess demand with buyers attracted by the double digit coupon of 10.25 percent but this is the final increase," syndicate manager at JP Morgan said.
"It was a very successful exercise and the deal has opened the sector for other institutions to follow."
The bond was originally launched on July 8 to yield 425 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
It was increased by $50 million at the same spread on July 10, and then again today by another $50 million at a spread of 420 b.p. over.
"The bond has tested 400 b.p. and has found a trading level between 410 and 400 bp over," JP Morgan's syndicate manager said.
Other Russian banks tipped to come to market soon are Alfabank and Uneximbank.
"The market is very much open for sensibly priced transactions," JP Morgan's syndicate manager said.
SBS-AGRO -- rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service, B+ by Standard & Poor's and BB by IBCA -- has the largest branch network of any private bank with 1,400 branches located throughout Russia.
